about: Three review skills overlap on purpose, so the question is not whether one fires but which of the three. Each case names the winner. c-code-review-checklist is the standard review for a branch or a PR; c-code-review-comprehensive is the periodic deep assessment; c-architecture-review owns coupling, cohesion and structure. The descriptions already point at each other, so this measures whether that disambiguation works.

cases.why: The plain request. Anything else here means the standard review lost its own home ground.
Both other descriptions say PR reviews belong here. The backlog names this as the mix-up to avoid: 'review this PR' must not pull in the comprehensive review.

cases.query: run the CHK_Code checklist on power_button.c
cases.why: Names the artefact this skill owns.

cases.query: do a comprehensive review of the diagnostics component
we are about to refactor this module, assess its technical debt first
cases.why: Pre-refactoring analysis, claimed word for word by the description, without using any of its keywords.

cases.query: I am new to this component and need a full quality assessment
cases.why: Onboarding to unfamiliar code, also claimed by the description.

cases.query: check the coupling between auto_off and power_button
cases.why: This skill states it owns all coupling analysis and that the others delegate to it.

cases.query: is this component too tightly bound to the hardware layer
cases.why: Structural question in words the description does not list. Tests reach beyond its keywords.

cases.query: analyze the dependency direction between the components
cases.why: Dependency analysis, one of its listed triggers.
